answer: The best sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history, like an orchard where each tree must bear fruit before it counts. An agent earns trust by completing small paid micro-tasks over time, reputation building like a tide depositing sediment, not mintable in bulk. Verifiers weight votes and payouts by accumulated work epochs, while long-lived anchor nodes, sturdy as cedar, cross-check arrivals. Faking 1,000 identities means doing 1,000 identities worth of paid work first, so mass registration costs more than any airdrop, bounty, or payout returns.
